Lessons.Title: Ways to Represent Measurement Situations
ExplanationParagraphs: Original 2021 Grade3 Unit6 Lesson12 is an open-ended fair/measurement modelling and TAPE-DIAGRAM lesson under CCSS3.MD.A.2. The owner-device archive's teacher lesson.html SHA256 705729bb4226ae4ce3e7b203ce667e7f4092c345bc4dda2e00c9baeb86008221 and preparation.html SHA256 fb7d8950d150453f93618fef896cce65fc061a40699b35177a20dc49b8f89d94 were individually inspected. Three public original student-facing task sections were reviewed. The downloadable Card Sort blackline master, original separately formatted pupil PDF and publisher photograph/card pixels were NOT found locally and not re-downloaded; full source parity of card matching remains open.

Warm-up Notice and Wonder The Fair (10minutes): three original photos depict state/county fair settings (carnival, produce/giant pumpkins, cows/animals). Invite multiple student observations and questions about activities, prices, weights and volumes. Do not require one specific numeric response to original open prompt. Original third-party photo files were not copied.

Activity1 Giant Pumpkin Event (20minutes): the original PHOTO is a prompt for pupils to WRITE A LIST of mathematical questions about giant pumpkins without given quantities. After discussion, the source teacher supplies EXACT source facts: smaller giant pumpkin weighs276 kilograms, larger giant pumpkin weighs347 kilograms. The teacher invites reasonable answerable questions. Two source-suggested families are HOW MUCH HEAVIER the larger is (347−276=71kg), and HOW HEAVY BOTH TOGETHER (347+276=623kg). Comparison may be phrased either 'how much less' or 'how much more', same positive difference71kg. These numeric answers derive from SOURCE TEACHER VALUES, not a claimed weighing of image pixels.

Activity1 teacher assigns ONE class-generated mathematical question to each PAIR, which may vary across groups. Pairs show their question, numbers, model and reasoning on a POSTER; teacher can let all groups answer same question or choose different source-compatible problems, then class performs a GALLERY WALK comparing diagrams. Do not claim pupils must solve BOTH the difference and sum questions if they were assigned only one. First-party examples illustrate common options without replacing learner-generated prompts.

Activity2 Card Sort: Giant Pumpkins (15minutes) gives each group of TWO a physical set of published SITUATION cards and matching DIAGRAM cards supplied from the teacher's BLACKLINE MASTER. Pupils match using tape-diagram segments and relational/equation reasoning, and explain WHY their match has the same underlying relationship. Source teacher explicitly confirms diagram C ↔ situation I: each seed packet weighs7 grams and all seed packets together weigh84 grams, so unknown number of packets is12, via ?×7=84 or84÷7=?. The source ALSO states diagram B ↔ situation E but does not print its complete numbers/card shapes in local narrative. Therefore B/E label matching can be preserved as SOURCE CONFIRMED while its underlying quantities/equations must NOT be fabricated. The rest of the card pairings and contents remain unverified without the original card master; teacher checks actual cards rather than arbitrary new matches.

Source MLR8 teacher supports partner verbal turns, an 'I noticed ____ so I matched ____' explanation scaffold, and chunking initial cards before revealing remaining ones. The source lesson synthesis asks why tapes, equations, equal groups, base-ten drawings or number lines suit measurements and their four operations, and how kilograms and liters communicate unit size. Note this source card set includes seed packets measured in grams even though lesson centers on giant pumpkins.

Original pupil PDF, source blackline card geometry, copyrighted photographs, gated publisher Cool-down Which Diagram Matches? and executed tests are NOT independently verified. This is A–B–C authored first-party companion with explicit source visual/teacher gates; no CI, Stage D, academic signoff, merge or deployment claimed.

KeyConcepts.Title: Weight difference
KeyConcepts.Definition: How much heavier one object is equals subtraction of the weights in same units.

KeyConcepts.Title: Combined weight
KeyConcepts.Definition: To combine two weights measured in same unit, add.
KeyConcepts.Example: The two original giant pumpkins weigh623kg altogether.

KeyConcepts.Title: Tape diagram matches story
KeyConcepts.Definition: Tape diagram parts and total should preserve original situation's units and relationships.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Check known segment amounts, repeated groups, total and unknown.

KeyConcepts.Title: Open modelling choices
KeyConcepts.Definition: Original lesson accepts several questions and valid solution representations.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Teacher grades assigned question, mathematical relation and coherent representation.
KeyConcepts.Example: One group compares 347 with276, another totals them.

WorkedExamples.Title: Source pumpkin difference
WorkedExamples.Question: How much more does 347kg pumpkin weigh than 276kg pumpkin?

WorkedExamples.Title: Source pumpkin total
WorkedExamples.Question: How heavy are original two pumpkins together?

WorkedExamples.Title: Source-confirmed card C and I
WorkedExamples.Question: Total84 grams; each pack7 grams. How many packs?
WorkedExamples.Method: Unknown number of equal parts on tape diagram.
WorkedExamples.Check: 12×7=84; C ↔ I in source teacher synthesis.

WorkedExamples.Title: Source-confirmed B and E
WorkedExamples.Question: How do source diagram B and situation E relate?
WorkedExamples.Method: Teacher visually compares original printed card texts and tape proportions.
Steps: Read the actual printed situation/card geometry.
Do not invent numeric values when unseen.
WorkedExamples.Check: Exact card equations remain teacher gated.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claim all pairs of publisher card deck are known from one teacher example.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Blackline master not present locally, and narrative exposes only C-I and B-E labels.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Preserve only verified labels, set remaining to teacher source-card review.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treat different pupil questions as wrong because not exact teacher's subtraction example.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Source students generate questions and teacher selects one for each pair.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Accept valid answerable weight questions and their models.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Confuse weight difference with combined mass.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Subtract and add are different relational questions.
